Why not refuse, measured by reading: Run commits a sequence first and writes the entry after (harness-core harness.rs:1777 then :1783; undo :1939 then :1944), so a session refusal would hit the Viewer's own edits and undos.

Inert keeps what can be checked without the owner: an absent sequence id keeps the key grammar, an absent track or clip id the domain id grammar with its own prefix (malformed is InvalidId, lead ruling 6), uniqueness, point counts and ranges, levels, send ids, budgets. A multicam mode of an absent clip keeps its SCLP grammar, uniqueness, follow rule and the angle ceiling MAX_MULTICAM_ANGLES, since it has no source to count against.
An id held with the wrong kind stays refused InvalidId: an envelope of a clip on a video track, a route of a video track, bus effects on an audio track.
An inert route is inert whole: its own output and send targets are not checked as references, and they keep the STRK grammar (lead ruling 6).

Consequence of the rule: a write may name an absent id, on Viewer::set_audio_routing and on a multicam step. A step writing a mode for a clip it does not hold commits (session multicam_commit.rs:372 removed).

Consequence: a new clip, track or sequence created with the id of an inert member takes that member. Tested for a track and a clip (an_inert_member_is_live_again_when_its_track_or_clip_exists). Clip and track ids are minted uuids; sequence ids are the caller's, not tested here: the lead records that case as an SD item and a validator probe.

A direct set_document_entry of audio_routing stays its producer's to validate, unlike settings: harness-core tests/run_and_entry_redo.rs:304 writes `{}` under this token. A file with such bytes is noted at the next open.
The records step does not carry audio_routing (lead decision 3). A bad routing is replaced by a direct write.

Listing shape: the requirement said codes and counters only, and following inert_track_display_entries. Studio reading: a kind code and an opaque id per row, no points, levels or names; a host could not act on a count alone. A whole absent sequence is one row. No Observe frame, as the other typed reads. The multicam listing returns the stored modes: ids, angle numbers and switches.

A repair undo: WithoutEntries(tokens) when other changes keep their undo; Unavailable(tokens) with no inverse when nothing else changed, or when the kept new records would not validate against the document the undo restores (a repair naming a sequence the same step inserts). In that second case the sequence edit has no undo either: the undo would be refused, and the answer says so rather than hand out a step that cannot apply. This is the one corner where item 4's "the sequence edit keeps its undo" does not hold.

The undo answer judges only records the step replaced: expect against the pre-step document. A sequence removal guarded later can still refuse an inverse for another entry written after the commit; that is the live state, not this answer.
Multicam guard on the records step still runs only on a Remove, as before; a Replace is not guarded, so Records Track stays in the gap.

Studio-minted, not in the spec: StudioInertRoutingKind and its members, StudioInertRoutingReference, SequenceRecordsUndo and its members, Applied::sequence_records_undo. Vendor parity UNVERIFIED (D5).
